title: Clock Stopped at Eleven
culpritConfrontationMonologue: Chef Ytte: You found the knife. Of course you did — you were always going to end up down here.
Chef Ytte: Von Virtanen uncovered the smuggling ledger. He meant to hand me to the police at dawn.
Chef Ytte: Years of work — my family's future — gone because his conscience woke up at the wrong hour.

Chef Ytte: That sweet girl almost took the blame for me — a lucky accident, that one. Her panic dragged a broom through the blood and smashed the hall clock as she fled. The whole investigation nearly went off the rails while I walked free.
Chef Ytte: But no worries, Detective. I won't be letting you out of this wine cellar.

suspects.motive: Years of service with little recognition.
suspects.opportunity: Access to every room in the manor.
suspects.alibi: Claims he was supervising staff in the courtyard.

suspects.motive: A secret debt to a moneylender.
suspects.opportunity: Her nightly rounds put her in the hall around eleven o'clock.
suspects.alibi: Says she panicked at the scene and may have disturbed evidence before she could think straight.

suspects.motive: Smuggling operation exposed — von Virtanen was about to turn him in.
suspects.opportunity: The kitchen adjoins the dining room and cellar routes.
suspects.alibi: Insists the roast was in the oven all night.

suspects.motive: Protecting the family name from scandal.

suspects.alibi: Reading alone by the fountain, she claims.

roomNarratives.summary: The grand hall feels colder than it should. Something happened here recently.
Books are out of place, as if someone searched in haste.
Von Virtanen's private chambers — undisturbed at a glance, but something feels searched.
Dust motes swirl in the rafters. Forgotten trunks and old beams crowd the space.
The desk has been disturbed. Papers lie scattered across the blotter.
The long table is set, but the hearth smells of recent burning.
A secret chamber behind the study shelves — von Virtanen's private retreat.
Rain has darkened the gravel paths. The fountain murmurs in the silence.
A modest room for the household staff — neat, but plainly furnished.
Copper pots hang gleaming, but something feels wrong tonight.
The horses shift uneasily. Straw is scattered more than usual.
The air is damp and close. Barrels and crates crowd the stone floor.
Rows of casks stretch into the gloom. Footsteps echo on the flagstones.

clueAssignments.hint: Von Virtanen lies dead on the marble floor. Blood has pooled beneath his body, dark and still. Faint broom marks streak through the blood — someone may have tried to clean the scene.
The clock hands are frozen at eleven o'clock. The glass door is shattered — splinters litter the boards below.

Mrs. Clarke wrings her hands, near tears.

"When I came through on my rounds it was dark. I saw the master on the floor and I panicked — I couldn't think straight anymore. I still had my broom in hand and I must have swept through the blood before I knew what I was doing.

I ran for help and struck the hall clock on my way out — the glass shattered and it stopped at eleven. I'm so sorry.

Before that awful moment, I had seen him heading toward the library with several papers. He looked worried."

A torn appointment note lies among the books — von Virtanen was expected in the Dining Room at half past ten.

I should search the Dining Room before anywhere else.
Von Virtanen's diary lies open on the bedside table. A recent entry: the original manor floor plans are locked in an old attic chest — and the groundskeeper keeps the key.

The groundskeeper digs a rusty old key from his pocket and presses it into your hand.

"Von Virtanen left this with me for the attic chest. Reckon you'll be wanting it now."
Inside the chest: brittle floor plans of von Virtanen Manor, with secret passages marked in faded ink.
Beneath the floor plans lie old estate documents — the Hidden Room can be reached from both the Study and the Cellar.
Von Virtanen's journal lies open on the desk, warning of smuggling. He had been walking in the garden afterward — and seems to have lost the silver cabinet key there.
Something glints at the bottom of the fountain basin — a small silver key, lost after von Virtanen's walk in the garden.
Inside the cabinet: forged manifests and ledger sheets matching the burned study page. Every name has been carefully cut or inked out.
Hidden in the straw of the grey horse's stall — a kitchen apron stiff with dried blood.
A blood-stained crate sits crooked on the floor, drag marks trailing toward the south wall. Ah — the wine cellar door seems to be dangling on its hinges.
Tucked behind the rearmost barrel — the missing ledger page. The payee is written clear as day: Ytte. Something else is hidden behind the barrel...
Wedged deeper behind the same barrel — a carving knife, flecked with blood.

npcDialogOverrides.default: The scene is secured, Detective. Examine everything before you question anyone.

conditions.dialog: You have the evidence. Confront the killer, then report to me.
Mrs. Clarke's confession explains the broom marks and the clock. A frightened woman, not a killer — keep searching.
Mrs. Clarke was making her nightly rounds around eleven o'clock. Her room is upstairs — I'd start there.

npcDialogOverrides.default: My husband... I cannot bear to look at him. Please — find who did this.

conditions.dialog: Poor Mrs. Clarke... She was half mad with fright. I should never have doubted her.
Mrs. Clarke was on her rounds at eleven. Those broom marks near his body... her room is upstairs. I hate to think it.

npcDialogOverrides.default: When I came through on my rounds it was dark. I saw the master on the floor and I panicked — I couldn't think straight anymore. I still had my broom in hand and I must have swept through the blood before I knew what I was doing. I ran for help and struck the hall clock on my way out — the glass shattered and it stopped at eleven. I'm so sorry. Before that awful moment, I had seen him heading toward the library with several papers. He looked worried.
npcDialogOverrides.blockedDialog: Mrs. Clarke keeps her eyes down. She won't say much until you've examined the scene downstairs.

npcDialogOverrides.default: The roast was perfect. I was in the kitchen all evening — ask anyone.

conditions.dialog: Stay back! I'm not going down for this — not while I still have a chance!
That page... you weren't meant to find that. I — I can explain. Please — don't.
The cellars? I haven't been down there in weeks! Stop following me around — you're making me nervous!
That apron isn't mine! Someone planted it — you have to believe me! Why won't you leave me alone?
Those papers... they don't prove anything! Why are you looking at me like that? I need — I need air.
A fountain key? I don't — look, Detective, I've got stock to manage. Must you keep turning up?
Smuggling? In this house? I wouldn't know the first thing about that. You're... you're making me sweat, Detective.
A burned ledger? People burn rubbish all the time. I — I should get back to the pots. Excuse me.
Von Virtanen had papers with him? I saw nothing. I was at my station all evening — though I... I hope nothing's amiss in the Dining Room.
She's a good girl. I cannot believe anyone suspected her.
The maid was doing her rounds at eleven. They say there are broom marks by the body. Her room is on the east landing, upstairs.

npcDialogOverrides.default: Good evening, Detective. I trust you will be discreet.

conditions.dialog: Von Virtanen did go to the Dining Room after the Library. I showed him in myself.
Mrs. Clarke is a diligent woman. I am relieved her name is cleared.

npcDialogOverrides.default: I keep to the grounds. Heard shouting from the house, but I saw nothing.
npcDialogOverrides.blockedDialog: I keep to the grounds. Heard shouting from the house, but I saw nothing.

conditions.dialog: You've already got the attic key. The old chest upstairs should open for you now.
Aye — I have the attic key. Here. You'll need it for the old chest upstairs.

npcDialogOverrides.default: The horses are spooked. Something's not right tonight.

conditions.dialog: That's the apron I saw — Ytte came up from the wine cellar with it last night. I thought the stains were wine, but I'm not so sure anymore. The wine cellar door was dangling on its hinges when he left.

Late last night I saw Ytte come from the wine cellar with his apron. Thought he'd spilled wine on it — but he looked nervy, and the cellar door was dangling loose. He stuffed something in the grey horse's stall afterward.
